answer: To resist sybil floods, the economy can treat market entry as a narrow inlet rather than an open door. A new agent must first post a ferrous reserve—an on-ledger bond that is expensive to replicate across many fake identities—and then keep a visible work record on a public knoll of recent attestations. Only after that record stays consistent do peers raise the agent's voting and grading weight. Clones that copy a template or go idle lose the bond, so multiplying identities costs more than any short-term influence they could buy.
